Therefore
THAIR-for
adv.
Middle English therefore: there + for. Webster 1828: for that; for that or this reason, referring to something previously stated; then consequently; then in return. His illustrations are Luke 14:20 (I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come) and Matthew 19:27 (What shall we have therefore?). The KJV uses it for the leaving of father and mother, for the expulsion from Eden, for justification’s peace, for no condemnation, and for the living sacrifice.

Biblical Definition

Therefore in Scripture is not a throat-clearing. It is the hinge that makes a doctrine become a life. Genesis does not treat marriage as a mood: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife (Gen 2:24) — the one-flesh union follows from how she was taken from him. Judgment has the same hinge: Therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden (Gen 3:23). Paul will not leave justification as a theory: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God (Rom 5:1). Union with Christ has a matching clause against the bench: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus (Rom 8:1). Mercy then commands a body: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice (Rom 12:1). The dictionary therefore keeps the adverb from becoming a filler between paragraphs. Where God has spoken a ground, He requires a consequence. No therefore, no obedience that knows why.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines THEREFORE as an adverb from there and for: for that; for that or this reason, referring to something previously stated; consequently; in return or recompense. He quotes Luke 14:20 and Matthew 19:27.

expand to see more

THEREFORE, adverb ther'fore. [there and for.] 1. For that; for that or this reason, referring to something previously stated. I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come. Luke 14:20.

2. Consequently. He blushes; therefore he is guilty.

3. In return or recompense for this or that. What shall we have therefore? Matthew 19:27. Webster will not let the adverb float. It always points back to a ground already laid.

Key Scripture

Genesis 2:24 — "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh."

Genesis 3:23 — "Therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken."

Romans 5:1 — "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:"

Romans 8:1 — "There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit."

Romans 12:1 — "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service."

Modern Corruption

Therefore is corrupted when doctrine is stored without obedience, when peace is claimed without justification, and when marriage’s therefore is replaced by a self-invented union.

expand to see more

The first corruption is a church that loves Romans without the hinge. Justification is collected as a comfort and never becomes Romans 12:1. Therapeutic religion wants peace as a feeling and drops the ground. Paul’s therefore in Romans 5:1 is peace through our Lord Jesus Christ after justification by faith — not calm as a technique.

The second corruption is to claim Romans 8:1 as a slogan for people still walking after the flesh as a rule of life. The verse is for those in Christ Jesus. Antinomian talk uses no condemnation to cancel holiness. Paul’s next move is the living sacrifice. The adverb is not a permission slip. It is the gospel becoming a walk.

The third corruption is to unhook Genesis 2:24. The therefore of marriage follows from the woman taken from the man, one flesh, father and mother left. Progressive readings replace that ground with consent-as-sufficient and sex-as-identity. The verse will not travel to a union God did not make. The adverb still points at Eden, not at the age.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Middle English therefore (there + for). Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek oun (G3767) at Romans 5:1 and Romans 12:1; Greek ara (G686) at Romans 8:1. Genesis 2:24 and Genesis 3:23 leave the English therefore itself untagged in this cache; no Hebrew number is minted for those two. Companion pages treat justification, peace, marriage, and condemnation; this page is the English adverb.

expand to see more

Greek oun (G3767) — therefore, then, so (Rom 5:1; Rom 12:1).

Greek ara (G686) — therefore, then, consequently (Rom 8:1).

Romans 5:1 tags Therefore as G3767 beside justified G1344 and faith G4102.

Genesis 2:24 and Genesis 3:23 untagged on the word therefore in this cache — no Hebrew number is invented.

Usage

"Therefore shall a man leave (Gen 2:24) — marriage follows from how she was made, not from the age’s script."

"Justified by faith, therefore peace with God (Rom 5:1); the adverb is not a mood."

"I beseech you therefore (Rom 12:1): mercies already given become a living sacrifice, or the doctrine was never heard."
